Procedure: Seeds were placed in a bag containing brick gravels, thoroughly rubbed for frictional purification, then washed and dried.
Seeds were heated in a pan until blackened and oily matter drained completely, then cooled and washed properly.
Tankana was heated till constant weight was obtained and stored in air tight container.
Raw Swarna Makshika was powdered and subjected to intense heating at 750–900 °C in a closed iron pan for 3 days until sulfur fumes ceased and the material turned red-hot.

Compound: Zinc Ore (Zinc Carbonate or Zinc Oxide)
